text:
alexa: heads up — seeing a spike of TLS errors for api.redwood.dev in eu-west-1. ALB is returning the default cert (CN=*.elb.amazonaws.com) instead of the customer SAN, lots of 526 / SSL handshake failures. :rotating_light:

sam: wow. did this start after the cert rotation last night?

marta: confirmed — metrics show spike at 07:42 UTC. logs show SNI coming in as "api.redwood.dev" but ALB is routing to the default listener cert. snippet from ALB access logs: 
```
TLS-Client-Cipher: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256, SNI: api.redwood.dev, SSL-Protocol: TLSv1.2, result: SSL handshake failure
```

jordan: are we terminating TLS at ALB or passing through to the ingress? I vaguely remember we moved some customers to TLS passthrough for mTLS.

alexa: we terminate at ALB for hosted traffic. private deploys sometimes use TCP passthrough. This is hosted though — should be ACM cert attached to the 443 listener.

sam: can anyone check ALB listener rules? If the host-based rule order is wrong, ALB might pick default cert. Also ensure the ALB has the SAN for api.redwood.dev in the certificate.

marta: checked ACM — cert for api.redwood.dev is valid and attached to the listener. But I noticed we have a TLS listener (443) with multiple certificates: one wildcard and one SAN cert. AWS picks cert based on SNI; if cipher or SNI isn't recognized it falls back to default. Could a client be using an older TLS stack?

leo: we saw some mobile clients with TLS1.0 attempts earlier but those should be rejected before SNI selection. More likely: ALB chooses certificate by SNI only when the client sends SNI in ClientHello. If our internal LB or proxy strips SNI (eg. TCP-level proxy) the ALB will fallback to default cert. Any chance our NLB->ALB chain is terminating TLS earlier?

infra-bot: Deploy 175.3.8 to kube-ingress started at 1753001100 by deploy-bot.

jordan: that deploy touched the ingress controller config. Could we have enabled proxy-protocol or altered the ELB annotations? Check `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme` and `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports`.

alexa: good catch — the ingress changes added an NLB in front of the ALB for fast path. I think the NLB is doing TLS passthrough but we accidentally set the target to a TLS-terminating ALB. That chain can remove the SNI header before ALB sees it.

sam: quick repro: curl with verbose to the ALB endpoint from inside VPC shows SNI present. But curl to the NLB IP then handshake shows no SNI in the logs. So NLB -> ALB chain is the culprit.

marta: immediate mitigation: update ingress annotation to have the ALB as the direct frontend (remove NLB) or configure the NLB to use TLS passthrough TCP with SNI preservation (not possible with classic NLB). Short term we can add a host-based rule that matches the default listener and routes to correct target group, but that still returns wrong cert.

leo: we can also add a dedicated TLS listener per host on the ALB and attach the exact ACM cert as the primary cert for that rule — ALB still uses SNI, but explicit listener certs are less ambiguous.

jordan: for customers using mTLS we need true TCP passthrough to the ingress pods (so the pod can do mTLS). That requires NLB/TCP to target the nodes directly; but for hosted endpoints we want ALB http/https termination. We need to ensure we don't chain them.

alexa: action items:
- roll back the ingress change that inserted the NLB (marta)
- audit ALB listener cert order and remove wildcard cert as default if it masks SANs (sam)
- add a canary rule to route a small subset of traffic to an ALB with single-certificate config to verify fix (jordan)
- run synthetic check from eu-west-1 to verify SNI and cert CN per-host (leo)

marta: I'll revert the ingress commit in 10m and open a PR to make the NLB opt-in with a config flag.

sam: repro note for oncall: check ALB access logs for "TLS-Client-Auth" and SNI field plus connection cipher; `aws elbv2 describe-listeners` will show certificates attached.

alexa: thanks — leaning on infra oncall to monitor errors and open an incident if errors don't drop under baseline by 08:30 UTC. tagging @oncall to watch. :eyes:

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-048 — edge-cert-sni-mismatch (severity: low -> watching).
